strings.d1.s0.name: Knossos Palace
strings.d1.s0.tips: The palace of King Minos and the labyrinth legend. Arrive for the 08:00 opening, as midday brings heat and tour groups. Note that Evans's restoration is controversial. Book tickets online.
strings.d1.s1.name: Heraklion Archaeological Museum
strings.d1.s1.tips: Minoan frescoes (the Prince of the Lilies, the Bull-Leaping fresco) and the Phaistos Disc. Air-conditioned.
strings.d1.s2.name: Heraklion Venetian Harbour & Koules
strings.d1.s2.tips: A Venetian fortress and a walk along the breakwater.
strings.d1.s3.name: Peskesi Heraklion
strings.d1.s3.tips: Cretan cuisine: dakos (barley rusk with tomato), staka (creamy dairy spread), wild greens, all farm-sourced.
strings.d1.s4.name: Lions Square & Morosini Fountain
strings.d1.s4.tips: The city centre. Try bougatsa (custard pastry) at Kirkor.
strings.d1.b0.name: Kirkor Bougatsa Heraklion
strings.d1.b0.tips: Serving bougatsa since 1922, with cream filling.
strings.d1.b1.name: Agios Minas Cathedral
strings.d1.b1.tips: The largest cathedral on Crete. An alternative to the harbour.
strings.d2.s0.name: Rethymno Venetian Harbour
strings.d2.s0.tips: On the way (1.5 hours by KTEL bus). Take in the Venetian lighthouse and narrow lanes.
strings.d2.s1.name: Fortezza of Rethymno
strings.d2.s1.tips: A 16th-century fortress with views over the Aegean.
strings.d2.s2.name: Taverna Knossos Rethymno
strings.d2.s2.tips: A family taverna by the harbour. Order the grilled fish.
strings.d2.s3.name: Chania Venetian Harbour
strings.d2.s3.tips: 1 hour by bus. See the Egyptian lighthouse, the Mosque of the Janissaries (Yali Mosque) and the Venetian shipyards (Neoria).
strings.d2.s4.name: Chania Old Town Topanas & Splantzia
strings.d2.s4.tips: The Turkish and Venetian quarters. Walk the leather street (Skridlof) and enjoy the evening lights.
strings.d2.b0.name: Tamam Chania
strings.d2.b0.tips: A restaurant in an old Turkish bathhouse serving Cretan-Ottoman food.
strings.d2.b1.name: Arkadi Monastery
strings.d2.b1.tips: A monastery tied to the 1866 resistance. Detour onto the mountain road from Rethymno (by car).
strings.d3.s0.name: Kissamos Port Balos Boat
strings.d3.s0.tips: No boats in winter. Go by jeep or car on the 8 km dirt road, then a 20-minute descent on foot. It is choppy but completely empty.
strings.d3.s1.name: Gramvousa Fortress
strings.d3.s1.tips: A Venetian fortress on the former pirate island. Expect a 137 m climb and a shipwreck.
strings.d3.s2.name: Balos Lagoon
strings.d3.s2.tips: The winter lagoon is for walking and wind. Swimming is for the brave.
strings.d3.s3.name: Kissamos Taverna Sunset
strings.d3.s3.tips: On the way back, stop at a seaside taverna in Kissamos for stifado (beef and onion stew) and local wine.
strings.d3.b0.name: Falasarna Beach
strings.d3.b0.tips: An ancient harbour and a long beach, ideal at sunset. An alternative to Balos (by car).
strings.d3.b1.name: Cellar Tavern Kissamos
strings.d3.b1.tips: A family taverna in central Kissamos. Lunch here if the boats are not running.
strings.d4.s0.name: Samaria Gorge Xyloskalo Entrance
strings.d4.s0.tips: The gorge is CLOSED in winter (flood risk). Alternatives: Imbros Gorge (8 km, open year-round) or the ancient city of Aptera.
strings.d4.s1.name: Samaria Abandoned Village
strings.d4.s1.tips: An old village halfway along the trail. Rest and refill your water.
strings.d4.s2.name: Iron Gates Sideroportes
strings.d4.s2.tips: The canyon narrows to 3 m here, its tightest point.
strings.d4.s3.name: Agia Roumeli
strings.d4.s3.tips: The coastal village where the gorge ends. Enjoy the sea and a taverna, then take the 17:30 ferry to Sougia or Chora Sfakion, and a bus on to Chania.
strings.d4.s4.name: Chora Sfakion Ferry Return
strings.d4.s4.tips: A ferry across the Libyan Sea, then a bus to Chania, arriving at 20:30.
strings.d4.b0.name: Imbros Gorge
strings.d4.b0.tips: An easy 8 km gorge walk, for when Samaria is closed or too demanding.
strings.d4.b1.name: Taverna Tarra Agia Roumeli
strings.d5.s0.name: Elafonisi Beach
strings.d5.s0.tips: The pink sand is empty in winter. Expect a windy walk.
strings.d5.s1.name: Elafonisi Taverna Innachorion
strings.d5.s1.tips: A taverna just behind the beach. Try the Cretan salad.
strings.d5.s2.name: Chrysoskalitissa Monastery
strings.d5.s2.tips: A white monastery perched on a rock, with the legend of the golden step.
strings.d5.s3.name: Topolia Gorge & Agia Sofia Cave
strings.d5.s3.tips: A canyon and a cave church on the way back.
strings.d5.s4.name: Chania Dinner To Maridaki
strings.d5.s4.tips: Seafood meze in Chania Old Town.
strings.d5.b0.name: Kedrodasos Beach
strings.d5.b0.tips: An empty cedar-lined beach next to Elafonisi, a 20-minute walk away.
strings.d5.b1.name: Milia Mountain Retreat Restaurant
strings.d5.b1.tips: Organic food in a mountain village. A detour.
strings.d6.s0.name: Plaka Spinalonga Boat
strings.d6.s0.tips: On the way back to Heraklion, turn east (by car or KTEL). The boat takes 5 minutes from Plaka (20 minutes from Elounda).
strings.d6.s1.name: Spinalonga Island
strings.d6.s1.tips: A Venetian fortress and a leper colony from 1903 to 1957 (the setting of the novel The Island). The walk takes 1 hour.
strings.d6.s2.name: Elounda
strings.d6.s2.tips: A luxury bay village. Try octopus at a harbour taverna.
strings.d6.s3.name: Agios Nikolaos Lake Voulismeni
strings.d6.s3.tips: The legend of the bottomless lake. Cafes and the harbour.
strings.d6.s4.name: Ammoudara Beach Heraklion
strings.d6.b0.name: Kritsa & Panagia Kera
strings.d6.b0.tips: A mountain village with Byzantine frescoes. An alternative to Agios Nikolaos.
strings.d6.b1.name: Ferryman Taverna Elounda
strings.d6.b1.tips: On the set of The Island, by the shore.
strings.d7.s0.name: Heraklion Central Market 1866 Street
strings.d7.s0.tips: Honey, olive oil, raki (tsikoudia), herbs and souvenirs.
strings.d7.s1.name: Nikos Kazantzakis Tomb
strings.d7.s1.tips: The author of Zorba the Greek. His gravestone on the walls reads 'I hope for nothing', with views over the city.
strings.d7.s2.name: Ippokampos Heraklion
strings.d7.s2.tips: A harbour taverna serving calamari and meze. A farewell meal.
strings.d7.s3.name: Heraklion Airport Bus
strings.d7.s3.tips: 15 minutes by bus or taxi. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Cretan Aquarium
strings.d7.b1.name: Phyllosophies Heraklion
strings.d7.b1.tips: A cafe on the square. Try the cakes.
strings.note0: Hiring a car is best (25-40 EUR/day), though KTEL buses run regularly between Heraklion, Rethymno and Chania. Three nights in Chania and two in Heraklion is ideal (the plan uses two bases).
strings.note1: From November to March Samaria is closed, there are no Balos boats (go by jeep) and Elafonisi is deserted. Expect a sunny 15°C winter and the olive harvest; April and May bring wildflowers and Easter.
strings.note2: Knossos costs 20 EUR (museum separate), Samaria 5, Spinalonga 8. Tavernas cost 15-25, with raki offered on the house. Round up the bill as a tip.
strings.note3: Cretan food: dakos, staka, kalitsounia (cheese pastries), snails (chochlioi), tsikoudia. Tap water is drinkable in Chania.
strings.note4: The Balos dirt road voids hire car insurance, so take a boat or a jeep. The ferry and bus back from Samaria arrive late.
strings.note5: Direct flights from Türkiye to Heraklion and Chania run in summer. A Schengen visa is required.
